title: Mitochondrial diseases
bottleneck: Mitochondrial disorders, caused by mutations in mitochondrial or nuclear DNA affecting energy production, have no curative treatments; heteroplasmy, the mixture of mutant and healthy mitochondria, and the blood-brain barrier complicate delivery, and editing mitochondrial DNA itself remains primitive.
why_it_blocks: These devastating, often childhood-onset diseases attack the highest-energy tissues, including brain, muscle, and heart, with only supportive care available.
current_state: Mitochondrial replacement techniques prevent transmission, and experimental mitochondrial gene editing is emerging. Treatments for affected patients remain supportive only, and delivery advances in the broader gene-therapy field have yet to reach mitochondria. Because mitochondria are inherited maternally and present in hundreds of copies per cell, even gene-editing successes face unique biological hurdles. Recent progress in mitochondrial DNA editing tools offers the first real hope, but clinical translation is years away.
